_: The audio pipeline's one table: what to cut, from what, to what.
`npm run audio` reads this, cuts each master with ffmpeg and writes the
encoded file beside it; `npm run build` refuses a stale or over-budget
one through scripts/check-audio.mjs. See docs/audio.md for the argument.
EVERY NUMBER HERE IS THE INPUT, not a record of what happened. The cut
lives in `trim` rather than in a binary somebody has to open, so the
shipped file is reproducible from a committed master and a reviewable
diff. `sourceHash` and `decoded` are the only fields the generator
writes back, and they are what the build gate checks.
The ceiling, in the unit that actually binds. A decoded AudioBuffer is
duration * ctx.sampleRate * channels * 4 bytes and NOTHING else -- the
container, the bitrate and the file's own sample rate are invisible to
it (measured: a 22 kHz file decodes back up to 48 kHz for identical
RAM). So the budget is seconds of mono, not bytes on disk.
44 s = 8 MB at 48 kHz, ~5% of the 157 MB heap FINDINGS.md #1 measures.
A stereo row spends two seconds of it per second of audio.
Cut to the REPORT and nothing after it. The master carries ~865 ms of
baked room -- a flat -18 to -24 dB plateau to 385 ms and then a slow
decay to -68 -- and Sfx already answers every gunshot with a shared
ConvolverNode on a send. Shipping the baked tail would double-reverb
the shot, put one fixed room on six maps, defeat botShot's
distance-climbing send, and hold a voice for 865 ms instead of 150.
Measured before cutting: the report's energy is gone by 130 ms (-8 dB
at 125, -20 by 135), and the 130-400 ms band has a crest factor of
6 dB with no window 5 dB above it -- dense noise, no discrete
reflection and no mechanism, so there is nothing in there to lose.
Stereo, which is the exception to the mono rule rather than a lapse:
the master carries real width (the side channel peaks 10.8 dB under
the mid, so it is not dual-mono), this is the one sample the player
hears UNPANNED as their own report, and at a 150 ms cut the second
channel costs 28 KB. The mono rule earns its keep on long sounds and
on anything only ever heard through a panner.
